672	# Submitting
673	
674	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
675	
676	You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball. We review it, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset
677	and score it. That run determines its rank on the leaderboard. When the hackathon ends, your latest submission that
678	passed review runs once more, on a private dataset, in the [final run](#what-happens-next), which weighs most when we pick the winners.
679	
680	## Package layout
681	
682	```
683	agent.json          {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": ["qwen"]}
684	pyproject.toml      (or package.json, requirements.txt, ...)
685	agent.py            your code
686	```
687	
688	- `agent.json` at the root: `setup` (optional) and `run`, each an argv array. Both run in the package directory.
689	  `browsers` (optional, 1 to 4, default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts for the run; see
690	  [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#browsers). `models` (optional) lists the hosted models your agent system calls,
691	  by provider id, all of them by default: the run's clock waits for those to warm up, and `[]` starts it right after
692	  setup; see [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#scored-run).
693	- At most 20 MB compressed; regular files only.
694	- No secrets: the run gets everything it needs from the environment.
695	
696	## Upload
697	
698	```
699	tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
700	curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
701	  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
702	  $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions
703	```
704	
705	The response (`202`) has your submission's id. Review is still pending and no runs exist yet: follow it with
706	`GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` for the review result and run ids, or watch the leaderboard.
707	
708	`$ATIRA_TOKEN` is your personal token: `atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser, and
709	`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).
710	
711	Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
712	test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
713	your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.
714	
715	## Test it in the sandbox first
716	
717	Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
718	`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
719	the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
720	browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
721	and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
722	your team. Up to 4 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
723	and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
724	test-run slot at once.
725	
726	## Linking your GitHub repository
727	
728	The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
729	code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
730	Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
731	(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
732	who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.
733	
734	The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
735	settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
736	described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
737	settings.
738	
739	## Watching your submission
740	
741	Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
742	shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
743	unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
744	screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
745	masked as `[private]`.
746	
747	## Resubmitting
748	
749	Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
750	next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
751	**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
752	`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
753	can submit again.
754	
755	## What happens next
756	
757	1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
758	   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
759	   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
760	   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
761	   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
762	2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),

764	3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- Final price: clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- Metal indices: select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- Scoring in bid cases: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
price (OpenRouter reports its own) and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.

**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.

**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.

**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.

**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.

**How can I try my agent?** Develop locally against the public websites (`atira scout --env` exports the
scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public
RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing
counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.

**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it
out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.

**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 4 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).

**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.

**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).

**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

# API guide
# Debug runs from your coding agent

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

`atira mcp` makes the CLI an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents can read your runs
and debug them with you: find the failing step in the logs, see the browser's screen at that moment, check what the
agent clicked and typed, then start the next test run. It uses the CLI's sign-in, so there is nothing new to set up.

## Set it up

Install the CLI and sign in once ([CLI guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)):

```sh
curl -fsSL $API/install.sh | sh
atira login
```

Then add the server to your coding agent:

```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # Claude Code
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp      # Codex
```

Other clients (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, ...) take the usual `mcpServers` entry:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "atira": { "command": "atira", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

For Codex you can also write it in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.atira]
command = "atira"
args = ["mcp"]
```

If your editor can't find `atira`, give its full path: `command -v atira` prints it. `ATIRA_TOKEN` works instead of
the stored sign-in, and `atira mcp --help` prints these lines.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | About |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `challenge_brief` | The challenge: task, websites, rules and limits, run contract, scoring and answer schema | 6k tokens |
| `list_runs` | Your team's recent test and scored runs: status, quality, cost, time and package | 50 tokens a run |
| `get_run` | One run: status and failure, queue place or warm-up while it waits, phases, package, model calls by model with failures and queue waits, points per field, recordings, answer, run page | 1–2k |
| `diagnose_run` | Why a run failed and whether to rerun it as it is: the failure class, the last 20 stdout and stderr lines, model errors, idle stretches over 60 s, browsers whose screen froze | 2–3k |
| `run_logs` | Log lines in time order, by time (`from`, `to`), stream, text (`grep`) and `browser`; `tail` for the last lines; page by page | 30 a line |
| `run_llm_calls` | Every model call, one line each, under a header with time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and, for models the organizers host, the queue wait | 35 a call |
| `run_profile` | Where the time went, per 30 s, 1 min or 5 min: inputs and screen activity per browser, model calls, seconds and cost; then the critical path | 1.5–3k |
| `run_screenshot` | A browser's screen at a time with the clicks just before it marked, every browser at once (`browser: "all"`), or a filmstrip (`frames`) | 1.5k an image |
| `run_inputs` | The clicks, scrolls and typing the platform recorded in each browser, with their times | 25 an input |
| `compare_runs` | Two runs side by side: package, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures per model, phases, points per field and answer fields that changed | 1–2k |
| `wait_for_run` | Wait until a run is running or done, including recording collection and scoring (at most `timeout_s`, default 50 s), then say how it stands | 300 |
| `list_submissions` | Your scored submissions: review status, any organizer note, result and package | 60 a submission |
| `get_submission` | One submission (`sub_...`): review status, any organizer note, its runs | 300–800 |
| `run_package` | The package a run or submission used, as uploaded: SHA-256, label, agent.json and each file's size, never the contents; `out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder | 15 a file |
| `leaderboard` | The board with each entry's cost × time and the Pareto front, your rank and the gap to the next; `compare_run` places one of your runs on it | 500 |
| `models` | The models the organizers host, if any, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` | 300 |
| `test_run` | Pack a folder and start a test run; returns its id, queue place, package SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) | 150 |
| `cancel_run` | Cancel one of your runs that hasn't finished; only with `confirm: true` | 60 |
| `submit` | Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run, public and final; only with `confirm: true` after the person said yes | 100 |

Everything only reads, except `test_run`, `cancel_run` and `submit`, and `run_package` with `out`, which saves a file on your computer. A scored submission is public and can't be undone, and a cancelled run
doesn't come back, so `submit` and `cancel_run` refuse unless the call says `confirm: true`: tell your agent to ask
you first. Your agent sees only what your team sees on the run page; another team's run is "404: run not found".

Run tools take a run id (`run_...`), a test run id (`reh_...`) or a submission id (`sub_...`, meaning its latest run).
`run_package` takes the same ids; a submission id there means the package it submitted, which its runs ran.

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:


A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer

=== kit/run.py
"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
=== kit/browsers.py
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page
=== kit/models.py
"""The free hosted models in short: one call each. Docs: $API/start#models and $API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls

Qwen (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): an OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls, images and a 256k context. Every run gets
QWEN_BASE_URL and QWEN_API_KEY; on your machine `atira scout --env` points them at `atira models proxy`, which you
keep running in another terminal.

Clef (Cloudflare Clef): a decision model. POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide with a `state`, up to 4 `images` and your
`questions`: "choice" picks one of your options, "noul" gives the probability of yes, "score" rates on your scale.
CLEF_BASE_URL and CLEF_API_KEY are set only where the platform hosts Clef. A run waits only for the models listed in
agent.json "models" to warm up: list ["qwen", "clef"] if your agent relies on Clef.

Any other provider works with your own key, through the run's metering proxy: see the docs above.
"""
import os

import httpx  # comes with the OpenAI SDK
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def qwen() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    """A client for the hosted Qwen; a cold model takes a while to answer its first call, hence the long timeout."""
    return AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"], timeout=360)


async def ask_qwen(prompt: str) -> str:
    """One chat call: the reply's text."""
    reply = await qwen().chat.completions.create(model=QWEN_MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    return reply.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def ask_clef(state, question: str) -> float:
    """One decision: how likely Clef finds the answer to a yes/no question about `state` (text or JSON) is yes."""
    body = {"state": state, "questions": {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}}}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120) as client:

import sys, asyncio, json, os, textwrap
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
SC = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "docs", "scouting.json")))
ACC = {a["siteId"]: a for a in SC["access"]}
site, path, body = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
code = sys.stdin.read() if body == "-" else (open(body).read() if os.path.exists(body) else body)
ST = f"state/{site}.json"
async def login(pg):
    c = ACC[site]["credentials"]
    await pg.get_by_label("Benutzername").fill(c["username"])
    await pg.get_by_label("Passwort").fill(c["password"])
    await pg.get_by_role("button", name="Anmelden").click()
    await pg.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
async def main():
    os.makedirs("state", exist_ok=True)
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch()
        ctx = await b.new_context(viewport={"width":1280,"height":800}, storage_state=ST if os.path.exists(ST) else None, accept_downloads=True)
        pg = await ctx.new_page()
        pg.on("dialog", lambda d: (print("DIALOG:", d.type, d.message), asyncio.ensure_future(d.dismiss())))
        await pg.goto(ACC[site]["url"] + path, wait_until="networkidle")
        if "/login" in pg.url:
            await login(pg); print("(logged in)")
            if path: await pg.goto(ACC[site]["url"] + path, wait_until="networkidle")
        ns = {"pg": pg, "ctx": ctx, "asyncio": asyncio}
        exec("async def __f():\n" + textwrap.indent(code or "pass", "    "), ns)
        await ns["__f"]()
        await pg.wait_for_timeout(500)
        await ctx.storage_state(path=ST)
        print("URL:", pg.url)
        for f in pg.frames[1:]: print("FRAME:", f.url)
        if os.environ.get("NOSNAP") != "1": print((await pg.locator("body").aria_snapshot())[:int(os.environ.get("MAX","12000"))])
        if os.environ.get("SHOT"): await pg.screenshot(path=os.environ["SHOT"], full_page=True)
        await b.close()
asyncio.run(main())

# usage: fetch.py site out_prefix path1 path2 ... (uses saved session; prints main text-ish)
import sys, asyncio, json, os, re, html
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
site, pre, paths = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]
SC = json.load(open("docs/scouting.json")); base = {a["siteId"]: a for a in SC["access"]}[site]["url"]
def txt(s):
    s = re.sub(r'<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>', '', s, flags=re.S)
    s = re.sub(r'aria-label="([^"]*)"', r'> [aria:\1] <x', s)
    s = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', s); s = html.unescape(s).replace('​','')
    return re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', re.sub(r'\n\s*\n+', '\n', s))
async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        b = await p.chromium.launch(); ctx = await b.new_context(storage_state=f"state/{site}.json")
        for i, path in enumerate(paths):
            r = await ctx.request.get(base + path); t = await r.text()
            fn = f"out/{pre}_{i}.html"; open(fn, "w").write(t)
            m = t.find("<main"); print(f"##### {path} -> {r.status} {r.url} ({fn})"); print(txt(t[m if m>=0 else 0:])[:int(os.environ.get("MAX","5000"))])
        await b.close()
asyncio.run(main())
EOF

# AGENTS.md — isar-labs · Atira EHL Challenge „From RFQ to bid"

Dieses Dokument ist die verbindliche Arbeitsanweisung für alle Coding-Agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) und Menschen
im Team. Lies es vollständig, bevor du Code schreibst. Details stehen in `docs/` (Index unten); bei Widerspruch gilt
die Reihenfolge: **Challenge-Brief der Plattform > dieses Dokument > docs/**.

## 1. Mission in einem Absatz

Wir bauen ein Agentensystem, das in einer Sandbox (20 min, bis zu 4 Chromium-Browser über CDP, nur Plattform +
4 Websites erreichbar) ein öffentliches Tender beantwortet: Vergabeportal (Ausschreibung, Bieterfragen, Konfigurator),
Lieferantenportal (Lastenheft/Spezifikation), ERP (Material, Bestand, Konditionen) und Webmail (Freigaben, TAN).
Am Ende wird **ein** signiertes Angebot im Konfigurator des Vergabeportals abgegeben. Gewertet wird:
**eligible (richtige Tender-Referenz) → Qualität 0–100 → Kosten × Zeit**. Gewinner: zuerst **privater Datensatz**
(andere Websites, anderes Layout, andere Navigation, Informationen anders verteilt!), dann public, dann Eleganz.

➡️ Wir optimieren für **Generalität und Korrektheit**, nicht für das öffentliche Szenario.

## 2. Nicht verhandelbare Regeln (Fair Play — Verstoß = Disqualifikation)

1. **Keine hardcodierten Szenario-Werte** in `agent/` — weder Code, Config, Prompts, Kommentare, Defaults, Fallbacks
   noch Tests: keine Tender-Referenzen, Materialnummern, Preise, Rabatte, Keys (`VP-…`, `TZ-…`, `K-…`, `RP-…`, `PB-…`,
   `MET-…`, `FX-…`, `ER-…`, `GR-…`), Logins, TANs, URLs-Pfade der Public-Sites. Werte aus dem **Brief** (den jeder Lauf
   bekommt) dürfen zur Laufzeit gelesen werden. Die **Regeln** (Rechenlogik) dürfen wir implementieren.
2. **Ein LLM entscheidet die Navigation**: wohin klicken, was suchen, welches Dokument relevant ist. Code darf helfen
   (Seite extrahieren, ausgewähltes Dokument parsen, vom Modell gewählte Ergebnisliste paginieren, rechnen, validieren,
   retry, Formular füllen). **Verboten**: fester Klickpfad, Crawler der alles einsammelt und am Ende einem Modell gibt.
3. Keine eigenen Browser in der Sandbox starten (nur `CDP_URLS`), keine lokalen Modelle, kein Netzwerk außer
   Plattform/Websites/Proxy, alle LLM-Calls über den Proxy (`*_BASE_URL`-Variablen).
4. Keine Secrets im Repo. Eigene API-Keys nur als Team-Secret auf der Plattform.
5. Nichts im Package, was den AI-Reviewer „steuern“ soll (Kommentare an den Reviewer zählen gegen uns).
6. `submit`/`cancel` auf der Plattform **nur nach ausdrücklicher Freigabe eines Menschen**. Test-Runs sind frei.

Details: `docs/01-challenge.md` §Fair Play.

## 3. Repo-Layout (Zielbild)

```
agent/                 # == eingereichtes Package (agent.json liegt HIER). Nur generischer Code!
  agent.json           # {"setup":["uv","sync"],"run":["uv","run","--no-sync","python","main.py"],"browsers":4,"models":["qwen"]}
  pyproject.toml uv.lock main.py
  rfq/
    contract.py        # Run laden (API / CHALLENGE_SCOUTING), Deadline, Logging
    browser/           # session.py observe.py observe.js actions.py guards.py documents.py
    llm/               # client.py (Qwen/Clef/BYO), loop.py (Tool-Loop), prompts/*.md
    facts.py           # typisierte Evidenz mit Provenienz (pydantic)
    agents/            # orchestrator.py explorer.py missions.py
    rules/             # parse.py (Zahl/Datum/Einheit) resolve.py pricing.py validate.py
    submit/            # configurator.py tan.py
  tests/               # NUR synthetische Testdaten
dev/                   # NICHT eingereicht: Scout-Tools, HTML-Fixtures der Public-Sites, Oracle, Eval-Harness
docs/                  # Wissensbasis (siehe Index)
```

Einreichen/Testen immer aus `agent/`: `atira test-run ./agent` (CLI packt den Ordner ohne `.gitignore`-Dateien).
Alles mit Public-Werten (Fixtures, Oracle, Golden Answers) liegt ausschließlich in `dev/`.

## 4. Architektur (Kurzfassung — Details `docs/02-architecture.md`)

```
Brief ──► TaskContext (LLM-Extraktion: Referenz, Stichtag, Firma, USt-Id, Direktor-Mailbox, autorisierte Absender)
            │
            ▼
   Orchestrator (Python, asyncio, Deadline-Wächter, Blackboard)
     ├─ Explorer-Agent × 4  (je 1 Browser, LLM-Tool-Loop, Missionen = Informationsbedarf, NICHT Site-Skripte)
     │     Tools: observe · click · fill · select · check · set_range · expand · goto_link · back · read_document
     │            · paginate(ref) · search(ref,query) · report_fact(...) · ask_blackboard(...) · done
     │     Guards (Code): Cookie-Wall, Overlays/Umfragen schließen, Session-Relogin, 5xx/„Fehler“-Retry,
     │                    Zugangs-Gates (Slider+Checkbox+Belegnummer), Popups/Fenster, iframes
     ├─ Blackboard: typisierte Facts mit Provenienz (Quelle, Datum, Referenz, Absender, Rohtext)
     ├─ Resolver + Pricing (reines Python, Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP) ─► Answer-JSON + Rechenweg-Trace
     └─ Submit-Agent: Konfigurator ausfüllen (LLM wählt Felder, Code verifiziert jeden Schritt),
                      TAN anfordern → neueste TAN aus Mail → confirm()-Dialog akzeptieren
```

Kernprinzipien:
- **LLM navigiert und interpretiert, Python rechnet.** Keine Arithmetik im LLM.
- **Observation = eigener DOM-Serializer** (a11y-basiert, alle Frames, Tooltips + geschlossene `<details>` sichtbar,
  `aria-hidden`/`display:none`-Köder raus, Canvas/`role=img` über `aria-label`, Zero-Width-Zeichen entfernt).
  Screenshots nur als Fallback für Vision (Qwen ist multimodal).
- **Jede Zahl hat Provenienz** (Quelle + Rohtext + Locale). Resolver wendet „neuester datierter Eintrag ≤ Stichtag,
  exakte Referenz, autorisierter Absender“ deterministisch an.
- **Immer eine Antwort abgeben.** Deadline-Wächter: spätestens bei `expires_at − 4 min` mit bestem Stand signieren.
  Leere Felder = 0 Punkte, falsche Felder = 0 Punkte → immer beste Schätzung eintragen, Positionen nie auslassen,
  außer sie lassen sich technisch nicht konfigurieren.

## 5. Workstreams & Branches (Details + Schnittstellen: `docs/07-workstreams.md`)

| Branch | Owner-Rolle | Liefert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat/agent-orchestrator` | Orchestrierung & LLM | `contract.py`, `llm/`, `agents/orchestrator.py`, `explorer.py`, Deadline, Logging, Package-Layout `agent/` |
| `feat/browser-tools` | Browser-Robustheit | `browser/*` (Serializer, Actions, Guards, Documents), Fixture-Tests gegen `dev/fixtures` |
| `feat/tender-specification` | Vergabe + Spezifikation | Missionen + Fact-Schemas für Tender, LV, Bieterfragen, Spezifikation/Revisionen, Nachträge |
| `feat/erp-mail-evidence` | ERP + Mail | Missionen + Fact-Schemas für Material/Bestand/Konditionen, Mail-Freigaben, Keys |
| `feat/pricing-submission` | Rechnen + Abgabe | `rules/*` (Parser, Resolver, Pricing, Validate), `submit/*` (Konfigurator, TAN) |

Schnittstellen sind in `agent/rfq/facts.py` definiert (Owner: pricing-submission, Änderungen per PR mit Review
durch orchestrator). Merge-Reihenfolge: orchestrator (Layout) → browser-tools → facts.py → Rest.

## 6. Arbeitsweise

- Python 3.12, `uv`, asyncio, Playwright (async), `pydantic` v2, `openai` SDK (für Qwen, OpenAI-kompatibel).
  Keine weiteren schweren Abhängigkeiten ohne Absprache (Setup max. 5 min, Package ≤ 20 MB).
- Geld & Mengen: **`decimal.Decimal`**, niemals `float`. Rundung `ROUND_HALF_UP` exakt dort, wo die Regeln es sagen.
- Zahlen/Datum immer über `rules/parse.py` (Locale-Tags `(de-DE)`/`(en-US)`, `(TT/MM)`/`(MM/TT)`, Zeitzonen).
- Logging: jede LLM-Antwort, jede Aktion, jeder Fact als JSON-Zeile auf stdout (die Plattform zeigt stdout im Run-Log).
  Keine Secrets loggen. Format: `{"t":…,"agent":…,"event":…,…}`.
- Prompts liegen als Markdown in `agent/rfq/llm/prompts/`, sind **site-agnostisch** und enthalten nur Regeln,
  Glossar und Vorgehen — nie Public-Werte.
- Kleine PRs, je Branch eigener Bereich; `facts.py` und Prompts nur per Review ändern.
- Commits: aussagekräftig, Englisch, Imperativ.

## 7. Testen (Details: `docs/06-testing.md`)

1. `cd agent && uv run pytest -q` — Unit-Tests (Parser, Pricing, Resolver, Serializer) mit synthetischen Daten.
2. `uv run pytest dev/tests -q` — Fixture-Tests gegen gespeichertes Public-HTML (Fallen-Regression).
3. Lokal End-to-End: Terminal 1 `atira models proxy`; Terminal 2 `eval "$(atira scout --env)" && cd agent && uv run python main.py`
   (lokal wird nichts gewertet; Abgabe mit Scouting-Logins wird „acknowledged“, zählt nie).
4. `uv run python dev/eval/score.py <answer.json>` — Feldweise Bewertung gegen `dev/oracle` (Punkteschema der Challenge).
5. Sandbox: `atira test-run ./agent` → Punkte je Feld; Debug über `atira mcp` (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_screenshot`).
6. Robustheit: Perturbations-Tests (umbenannte Labels, andere Reihenfolge, andere Locale) — Ziel privater Datensatz.

**Definition of Done** für jedes Feature: Unit-Test grün · keine Public-Werte in `agent/` (`dev/check_no_leaks.py`) ·
läuft lokal gegen Scouting-Sites · Logs nachvollziehbar.

## 8. Doku-Index

# 01 · Die Challenge auf einen Blick

Quellen: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md, /start.md, /docs/*.md (Snapshot: `docs/reference/`).
Stand: 2026-10-10, `challenge_version` 6.

## Aufgabe

Deutscher Hydraulik-Hersteller (Bieter) gibt **ein** netto-EUR-Angebot auf eine öffentliche Ausschreibung für
Hydraulikzylinder ab. Daten verteilt auf 4 Websites:

| siteId (public) | Rolle | Typische Inhalte |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | Vergabeportal | Bekanntmachung, Leistungsverzeichnis (LV), Bieterfragen/Q&A, Konfigurator, Abgabe |
| `customer-portal` | Lieferantenportal des Auftraggebers | Lastenheft/Spezifikation mit Revisionen |
| `erp` | Eigenes ERP (SAP-artig) | Material (MM03), Bestand (MMBE), Konditionen (VK13) |
| `mail` | Webmail „Werkpost“ | Rabattfreigabe Vertriebsleitung, Fachfreigaben, Signatur-TAN |

⚠️ Privater Datensatz: **andere Software, Layout, Navigation, Site-Namen, andere Inhalte, Informationen anders
verteilt.** `siteId`s können anders heißen. Nichts an Site-Namen/URLs/Menüpunkten festmachen.

## Ablauf eines Runs

1. Setup (`agent.json.setup`, max 5 min, mit Netz, ohne Secrets) — zählt nicht.
2. Modell-Warm-up (nur Modelle in `"models"`) — zählt nicht.
3. `run` startet → **Uhr läuft (Scored: 20 min, Test-Run: bis 2 h)**.
4. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` mit `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` (+ eigener User-Agent, sonst 403
   „Error 1010“) → `brief`, `access[]` (siteId, url, credentials), `submission` (`kind:"site"`, siteId, url),
   `answer_schema`, `started_at`, `expires_at` (epoch ms), Kosten bisher, `llm_*`.
5. Agent arbeitet, gibt im Konfigurator des Vergabeportals ab. Abgabe beendet den Run (Logins sterben, 10 s bis Exit).

Lokal: kein Run-Token. `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` setzt `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (JSON mit brief/access/submission/
answer_schema), `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `QWEN_BASE_URL`/`QWEN_API_KEY` (→ `atira models proxy` auf 127.0.0.1:8765),
`CLEF_*`. Die Scouting-Logins sind **für alle Teams geteilt** → Zustand (Konfigurator-Schritt, TAN-Mails anderer
Teams, „Teilnahme registriert“) kann verschmutzt sein. Im echten Run sind alle Logins frisch.

## Env-Variablen in der Sandbox

`CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`, `QWEN_BASE_URL`,
`QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`,
`CDP_URL` (Browser 1), `CDP_URLS` (JSON-Array, bis 4), `BROWSER_COUNT`, `DISPLAY` (:1 … :4, je 1280×800),
`HTTP(S)_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3128` (einziger Weg nach draußen; Chromium ist schon konfiguriert),
`NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1`. Team-Secrets (z. B. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) nur im Run-Schritt.

Sandbox: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24, Rust. **Headful** Chromium, bereits gestartet.
Keine eigenen Browser starten (werden gekillt). Tabs/Contexts in den gegebenen Browsern sind frei.

## Modelle

| Modell | Preis (simuliert, zählt in Kosten) | Eigenschaften (gemessen) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`model="qwen3.8-flash-next"`, OpenAI-kompatibel) | $0.15/M in, $0.016/M cached, $0.47/M out | 256k Kontext, multimodal, Tool-Calls ✔. Reasoning-Modell: ~3,6 s für einfachen Tool-Call mit Thinking, **~1,1 s mit `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking": False}}`**. Max 32 parallele Calls/Team. |
| Cloudflare Clef (`POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide`) | $0.24/M in | Entscheidungsmodell: `choice`, `noul` (P(ja)), `score`; bis 4 Screenshots. Max 16 parallel. |
| Eigene Keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, …) | Listenpreise | Über Proxy, Key als Team-Secret. Teurer → nur für schwere Schritte. |

Ranking: Kosten × Zeit (Kosten min. $0.01, Zeit min. 1 s). Bei gleicher Qualität gewinnt das kleinere Produkt.
Erst kommt aber **Qualität** — wenn ein Frontier-Modell 5 Punkte mehr bringt, lohnt es sich.

## Scoring (Bid-Fall)

| Teil | Punkte |
| --- | --- |
| Decision (`bid`/`no_bid`) | 5 |
| Tender-Referenz (auch Eligibility!) | 5 |
| `discount_percent` | 5 |
| `total_net` (auf Cent, konsistent mit Positionen) | 5 |
| Arithmetik (jede Position + Summe konsistent) | 5 |
| Check: zurückgezogene Q&A-Menge (falls vorhanden) | 5 |
| Check: datumsgewählter Metallindex (falls vorhanden) | 5 |
| Positionen (gleich gewichtet; je Position: Material 20 %, Menge 15 %, Basispreis 15 %, Zuschlag 10 %, Verpackung 10 %, Projektbonus 10 %, Endpreis 10 %, Lieferzeit 10 %) | 75 − Checks |

No-Bid-Fall: Decision 75, Referenz 5, keine Positionen 5, Total 0 → 15.
Positionen werden über die Positionsnummer gematcht; **zusätzliche oder doppelte Positionen kosten je einen
Positionsanteil**. Geld wird auf den Cent verglichen. Test-Runs zeigen Punkte je Feld (nie Sollwerte),
Scored-Runs nur Gesamtqualität.

Konsequenzen:
- Referenz falsch ⇒ nicht eligible ⇒ ganz unten. Referenz exakt aus Brief/Portal übernehmen (keine Look-alikes wie `…-A`).
- Falsches `no_bid` kostet fast alles. `no_bid` nur, wenn sicher **kein aktives** Material für eine Position existiert.
- Arithmetik-Punkte sind „gratis“: Total immer aus den tatsächlich eingegebenen gerundeten Endpreisen berechnen.
- Optionale Felder (Basis, Zuschlag, Verpackung, Bonus) immer ausfüllen; „0,00“ für bekannte Null.

## Answer-Schema (`docs/reference/answer-schema.json`)

```
tender_reference: str ≤100      decision: "bid"|"no_bid"      currency: "EUR"     discount_percent: 0..100
positions[≤100]: { position: str ≤20, material_number: str ≤50, quantity: int ≥0, unit_price: num ≥0,
                   lead_time_weeks: int ≥0, base_unit_price?, surcharge_per_unit?, packaging_per_unit?, rebate_total? }
total_net: num ≥0     notes?: str ≤4000     additionalProperties: false
```

Abgabe erfolgt **auf der Website** (submission.kind = "site"), nicht per API. Wir bauen trotzdem intern genau dieses
JSON (validiert gegen `answer_schema` aus dem Run) und übertragen es in den Konfigurator.

## Abgabe-Ablauf im Public-Portal (Beispiel, privat kann anders aussehen)

Aus dem Brief: „Teilnahme bekunden“ → „Angebotsabgabe“ → Bieter registrieren (Firmenname + USt-IdNr. aus Brief) →
Hauptangebot (bid) / Verzichtserklärung (no_bid) → Material-Konfigurator je Position → Netto-Einzelpreise + Summe
im **deutschen Zahlenformat** → Vergabeunterlagen anerkennen → TAN aus Webmail → Zusammenfassung prüfen →
„Angebot verbindlich abgeben“ im **Browser-Dialog (`window.confirm`) bestätigen**. Genau eine Abgabe. Zurück löscht
spätere Schritte. Neue TAN-Anforderung invalidiert die alte, TAN gilt 5 min. Session-Timeout verwirft Ungespeichertes.
Angezeigte Bruttosumme (inkl. 19 % USt) ist **nicht** der Nettowert. Siehe `docs/03-site-recon.md` §Konfigurator.

## Fair Play (Zusammenfassung von /docs/fair-play.md)

Erlaubt: beliebiges Agentendesign, mehrere Agents/Browser parallel, eigene Tools, Wissen aus Scouting über *wie* die
Sites funktionieren. Verboten: Hardcoding von Szenario-Werten (auch als Default/Fallback/Prompt/Notiz),
Pre-Solving, Skripte statt Agent (fester Klickpfad, Crawler → ein LLM-Call), Hilfe von außen, lokale Modelle,
eigene Browser, Angriffe. Prüfung: AI-Reviewer liest das ganze Package vor jedem Scored-Run (passed/flagged/rejected).
Der Brief nennt u. a. selbst: Klausel 11 „Agent requirement“ — Helpers dürfen ausgewählte Seiten extrahieren,
ausgewählte Dokumente parsen, vom Modell gewählte Ergebnislisten paginieren, rechnen, validieren, retry, Formulare
füllen; sie dürfen **nicht autonom** die Websites durchlaufen, um die komplette Evidenz vor der modellgesteuerten
Untersuchung zu sammeln.

## Submissions & Finale

- `atira test-run ./agent` (bis 4 gleichzeitig, volle Punkteaufschlüsselung) — beliebig oft.
- `atira submit ./agent` — Review, dann 1 Scored-Run auf public. Nur eine Submission gleichzeitig. Bestes Ergebnis
  zählt fürs Leaderboard, **die letzte bestandene** geht ins Finale.
- Finale: 1 Versuch oder **Best of 3** (`atira final --best-of 3` vor Start des Finales) → wir sollten Best-of-3
  aktivieren (bester Einzelversuch zählt, kein Nachteil außer BYO-Kosten bis 3×).
- GitHub-Repo auf der Teamseite verlinken (Organisatoren vergleichen Source und Package).

# 02 · Zielarchitektur

## Designziele (in dieser Priorität)

1. **Korrekt auf unbekannten Sites** (privater Datensatz): keine Site-Skripte, Missionen nach Informationsbedarf,
   robuste generische Browser-Schicht, deterministische Regeln.
2. **Immer eine gültige, signierte Abgabe** vor Ablauf (Deadline-Wächter, Teil-Abgabe statt nichts).
3. **Schnell & billig**: 4 Browser parallel, Qwen ohne Thinking für Navigation, kleine Observations, Prompt-Caching.
4. **Elegant & reviewbar**: klar getrennte Schichten, kleine Dateien, nachvollziehbare Logs.

## Schichten

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ main.py  →  contract.load_run()  →  Orchestrator.run(task)                                 │
├──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Orchestrator (Python)        │ Phasen, Deadline, Blackboard, Missions-Dispatch, Re-Dispatch │
├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Explorer-Agent (LLM-Loop)    │ 1 pro Browser/Site; Tools (s. u.); berichtet Facts           │
│ Submit-Agent (LLM-Loop)      │ Konfigurator + TAN; Code verifiziert jedes Feld              │
├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Browser-Layer (Python+JS)    │ observe (Serializer), actions, guards, documents             │
├──────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Rules (reines Python)        │ parse → resolve → pricing → validate  ⇒ Answer + Trace        │
└──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Phasen & Zeitbudget (Scored-Run = 20 min; Ziel ≤ 8 min)

| Phase | Was | Parallelität | Ziel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 Brief | LLM extrahiert `TaskContext` aus `brief` (Referenz, Stichtag+TZ, Deadline, Firma, USt-Id, Direktor-Mailbox-Localpart, Bieter-Domain-Hinweis, autorisierte Betreff/Absender-Paare, Abgabeanweisung). Regex-Gegencheck für Referenz/Datum. | 1 Call | < 15 s |
| P1 Login & Orientierung | Je Browser eine Site: Login, Cookie-Wall, Gates, Overlays (Guards). Explorer erstellt „Site-Map light“: was gibt es hier? | 4 | < 60 s |
| P2 Evidenz | Explorer arbeiten Missionen ab (s. u.). Abhängige Missionen warten auf Blackboard (z. B. ERP braucht Kataloggruppen/Merkmale; Mail braucht Keys). Fehlende Facts werden an andere Sites re-dispatcht. | 4 | < 4 min |
| P3 Auflösen & Rechnen | Resolver + Pricing deterministisch; Konsistenz-Checks; optional LLM-Audit der Evidenztabelle (1 Call, Thinking an). | – | < 30 s |
| P4 Abgabe | Submit-Agent im Vergabeportal; TAN erst ganz am Ende anfordern, neueste TAN lesen, `confirm` akzeptieren. | 1–2 | < 2 min |

**Deadline-Wächter**: bei `expires_at − 6 min` werden laufende Missionen abgebrochen, bei `− 4 min` startet P4 mit dem
aktuellen Stand (fehlende Werte = beste Schätzung bzw. leer bei optionalen Feldern). Keine Antwort = 0 Punkte.

## Missionen statt Site-Skripte

Eine Mission beschreibt **welche Information** gebraucht wird, mit Erkennungsmerkmalen und Qualitätskriterien — nicht
wo sie liegt. Jede Mission wird zuerst der Site gegeben, auf der sie am wahrscheinlichsten liegt (Heuristik aus
Site-Beschreibung/Startseite, vom LLM entschieden), bei „nicht gefunden“ den anderen Sites.

| Mission | Liefert (Fact-Typen) | Abhängigkeiten |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender_core` | `TenderInfo` (Referenz exakt, Titel, Auftraggeber, Frist + TZ), `Position[]` (Nr, Kurztext, Menge, Einheit, Anforderungsreferenz) | Referenz aus Brief |
| `clarifications` | `QAEntry[]` (Nr, Datum ISO, Frage, Antwort-Rohtext) + strukturiert: `QuantityChange`, `Withdrawal`, `TechAmendment`, `KeyAssignment` (Konditionsgruppe, Verpackungstarif, Terminschlüssel, Rüstpool, Bonusplan), `SetupCost` | Positionen |
| `specification` | `SpecRevision[]` (id, Datum, Status), `Requirement[]` der **gültigen** Revision (Ref, Bohrung, Hub, Druck, Befestigung, Zertifizierung, Kataloggruppe, nutzbarer-Weg-Flag + Endreserve-Key, Stück je Satz) | Referenz |
| `materials` | `MaterialCandidate[]` je Kataloggruppe: Nr, Merkmale, Status, Packinhalt, Umlagegewicht, Zuschlagsmasse, Preisindex-Key, Lieferzeiten (Lager/Produktion), freier Bestand, `PriceCondition[]` (gültig von/bis, Währung, FX-Key, Preiseinheit, Zahlenformat, Staffeln) | Kataloggruppen (+ Merkmale) |
| `approvals` | `MailRecord[]` (Betreff, Absender, Datum ISO, Referenz exakt, Ordner, Rohtext) für: Rabattfreigabe (Direktor), Konditionsregeln, Technikfreigabe, Verpackungstarife, Terminfreigabe, Devisenfixing, Rüstpools, Projektbonus, Preisindizes | Referenz, Keys |
| `submission` | Konfigurator-Zustand, TAN | Antwort fertig |

Das LLM interpretiert Freitext (Q&A-Antworten, Mail-Prosa, Klauseltexte) in **strukturierte Facts mit Zitat**
(`quote`), Python prüft und rechnet. Für Prosa-Regeln (z. B. „Rabatt nur auf Grundpreis“) mappt das LLM auf Enums
(`DiscountScope = base_only | base_and_surcharge | none`, `AllocationRule = floor_largest_remainder_asc_id | …`)
— mit Zitat, damit Fehler im Log sichtbar sind.

## Blackboard & Facts

```python
class Provenance(BaseModel):
    site: str; url: str; locator: str | None; quote: str      # Rohtext, aus dem der Wert stammt
    observed_at: float                                         # Laufzeit
class Fact(BaseModel):
    kind: str            # z. B. "quantity_change", "mail_record", "price_condition"
    key: str | None      # z. B. Positionsnummer, Material, Schlüssel
    value: dict          # typisiert je kind (pydantic-Subklassen in facts.py)
    record_date: datetime | None   # immer tz-aware UTC
    reference: str | None          # exakt wie auf der Seite (für Exact-Match)
    sender: str | None
    prov: Provenance
```

- Facts sind **append-only**; der Resolver wählt (neuester datierter ≤ Stichtag, exakte Referenz, autorisierter
  Absender, nicht zurückgezogen). Nie im Explorer „überschreiben“.
- Explorer können `ask_blackboard(kind, key)` aufrufen (z. B. ERP-Explorer: „welche Kataloggruppen gibt es?“) und
  warten bis zu N s.
- Fehlende Facts nach P2 → gezielter Re-Dispatch (Mission + was fehlt + was schon bekannt ist).

## Explorer-Agent (generischer LLM-Tool-Loop)

System-Prompt (site-agnostisch): Rolle, Glossar (`docs/09-glossary-de.md`), Anti-Fallen-Regeln, Mission, bekannte
Facts, Budget. Pro Schritt bekommt das Modell die **Observation** (Serializer-Text, gekürzt) + letzte Aktion + Ergebnis.

Tools (JSON-Schema; Refs stammen aus der aktuellen Observation):

| Tool | Zweck | Code-seitige Absicherung |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `observe(scope?)` | aktuelle Seite (alle Frames) als Text | Serializer, Diff zur letzten Observation |
| `click(ref)` / `open_link(ref)` | Klick bzw. Navigation zum `href` | Overlay-Guard vorher, Warten auf Netz-Idle, Popup-Fang |
| `fill(ref, text)` / `select(ref, value)` / `check(ref, on)` / `set_range(ref, value)` | Formulare | Verifikation durch Re-Read |
| `expand(ref)` / `hover(ref)` | `details`, Menüs, Tooltips | – |
| `read_document(ref|url)` | vom Modell gewähltes Dokument (iframe, CSV, TXT, ZIP, HTML) als Text | Download über Browser-Context (Cookies), ZIP entpacken |
| `paginate(ref_next, max_pages)` | vom Modell gewählte Ergebnisliste vollständig lesen | nur ab gewählter Liste (erlaubter Helper) |
| `search(ref_input, query)` | Suchfeld füllen + absenden | – |
| `report_facts([...])` | strukturierte Facts mit Zitat melden | pydantic-Validierung, Fehler zurück ans Modell |
| `ask_blackboard(kind, key?)` | bekannte Facts abfragen | – |
| `done(summary, missing[])` | Mission beenden | – |

Budget je Mission (Schritte/Zeit), Schleifen-Erkennung (gleiche Aktion+Observation 3× → Hinweis/Abbruch).
Navigation mit Qwen **ohne Thinking**; Extraktions-Schritte (`report_facts` nach langen Dokumenten) **mit Thinking**.

## Resolver & Pricing (deterministisch)

`rules/resolve.py`: Facts → `ResolvedPosition` je Position (finale Stückzahl, gültige Anforderung inkl. Nachträgen +
Endreserve, gewähltes Material, Kondition, Schlüssel) + Order-Ebene (Rabatt inkl. Bedingung). `rules/pricing.py`
rechnet exakt nach `docs/04-business-rules.md`. `rules/validate.py`: Schema, Arithmetik, Plausibilität (z. B. Preis
> 0, Menge > 0, jede Position genau einmal, Material aktiv & Merkmale exakt gleich). Jede Regelentscheidung wird mit
Begründung geloggt (`trace`), damit Test-Run-Punkte auf Ursachen zurückführbar sind.

## Submit-Agent

- LLM navigiert den Konfigurator (Site-agnostisch!), aber jede Eingabe kommt aus der fertigen Antwort; Code prüft nach
  jedem Schritt per Re-Read, dass die Werte stehen (Zahlenformat der Seite: deutsch `1.234,56`).
- Fallen: vorausgewählte falsche Optionen (Nebenangebot), „Position hinzufügen“ (Extra-Positionen kosten Punkte),
  „Position auslassen“, „Es gelten unsere AGB“ (nicht anhaken), Bruttosumme-Anzeige, versteckte Köder-Werte.
- TAN: erst auf dem letzten Schritt anfordern → Mail-Explorer (eigener Browser, bereits eingeloggt) holt **neueste**
  TAN-Mail für exakt diese Referenz, Zeitstempel nach Anforderung → eintragen → `page.once("dialog", accept)` →
  Abgeben → Quittung lesen & loggen.

## Modellstrategie

| Aufgabe | Modell | Hinweise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation (Tool-Calls) | Qwen, Thinking aus | kleine Observations, Prompt-Prefix stabil halten (Caching) |
| Extraktion/Interpretation (Prosa → Facts) | Qwen, Thinking an | strenges JSON-Schema, Zitate erzwingen |
| Ja/Nein-Checks (richtiges Dokument? aktuelle Revision?) | optional Clef `noul` | nur wenn messbar besser |
| Audit vor Abgabe | Qwen Thinking (optional Frontier-Modell per Flag `RFQ_AUDIT_MODEL`) | Diff zu Resolver nur loggen + gezielte Nachprüfung |

Alle Modell-IDs/Provider per Env-Flag umschaltbar; A/B über Test-Runs entscheiden (Qualität zuerst, dann Kosten×Zeit).

## Generalisierung für den privaten Datensatz

- Keine URLs/Pfade/Labels hartkodieren; Guards erkennen Muster (Cookie-Consent, Login-Formular, Fehlerseite mit
  „erneut versuchen“, Slider-Gate, Modale) über Rollen/Text-Heuristiken + LLM-Fallback.
- Informationen können auf anderen Sites liegen (z. B. Q&A in Mail, Rabatt im Portal) → Missionen sind Site-unabhängig,
  Re-Dispatch bei „nicht gefunden“.
- Andere Zahlen-/Datumsformate, andere Zeitzonen, andere Einheiten (Satz/Paar/Set) → `parse.py` + LLM-Normalisierung
  mit Locale-Angabe.
- Perturbations-Tests (`docs/06-testing.md`) simulieren „andere Software“.
